i: 한글의 기본 모음 여섯 개입니다. 모음만 쓸 때는 앞에 소리 없는 ㅇ을 붙입니다.
These are the six basic vowels of Hangul. When you write a vowel alone, put a silent ㅇ in front of it.
w: My tooth hurts. I'm going to the dentist.
It is raining. Do you have an umbrella?
tp: ㅏ ㅓ ㅣ는 자음의 오른쪽에, ㅗ ㅜ ㅡ는 자음의 아래에 씁니다.
ㅏ ㅓ ㅣ are written to the right of the consonant, and ㅗ ㅜ ㅡ are written below it.
For ㅓ, open your mouth a little; for ㅗ, round your lips. English has no exact ㅓ: it is between the "o" in "hot" and the "u" in "cup". ㅗ is like the "o" in "go", but without the "w" at the end.
For ㅓ, open your mouth a little; for ㅗ, round your lips. English has no exact ㅓ: it is between the "o" in "hot" and the "u" in "cup". ㅗ is like the "o" in "go", but without the "w" at the end.
sm: 기본 모음은 ㅏ ㅓ ㅗ ㅜ ㅡ ㅣ 여섯 개입니다.
There are six basic vowels: ㅏ ㅓ ㅗ ㅜ ㅡ ㅣ.
qz: 자음의 아래에 쓰는 모음은? ㅏ / ㅗ / ㅣ

i: ㅐ와 ㅔ입니다. 요즘 한국 사람은 두 소리를 거의 같게 냅니다.
These are ㅐ and ㅔ. Today, Korean people say these two sounds almost the same way.
w: My stomach hurts, so I take medicine.
I learn Korean with Korean songs.
to know (알겠어요 = I see, I understand)
I buy crabs at the market.
tp: Both sound like the "e" in "bed" (ㅐ used to be more open, like the "a" in "cat"). It is OK if you cannot hear the difference. Learn them by their spelling.
Both sound like the "e" in "bed" (ㅐ used to be more open, like the "a" in "cat"). It is OK if you cannot hear the difference. Learn them by their spelling.
"네"는 대답하는 말이고, "내"는 "나의"라는 뜻입니다.
"네" is an answer (yes), and "내" means "my".
sm: ㅐ와 ㅔ는 소리가 거의 같아서 글자로 구별합니다.
ㅐ and ㅔ sound almost the same, so we tell them apart by spelling.

i: 기본 모음에 획을 하나 더하면 앞에 [y] 소리가 붙습니다.
If you add one more stroke to a basic vowel, a [y] sound (as in "yes") comes in front.
w: I saw a fox at the zoo.
The women's restroom is this way.
I am good at cooking Greek food.
The milk is in the fridge.
to know (알겠습니다 = I see, I understand)
Yes, I will come at nine o'clock tomorrow.
tp: ㅏ → ㅑ, ㅓ → ㅕ, ㅗ → ㅛ, ㅜ → ㅠ처럼 짧은 획이 두 개가 되면 [y]가 붙습니다.
ㅏ → ㅑ, ㅓ → ㅕ, ㅗ → ㅛ, ㅜ → ㅠ: when one short stroke becomes two, a [y] sound comes in front.
문장 끝의 "요"는 공손한 말투를 만듭니다. 아주 자주 듣게 됩니다.
"요" at the end of a sentence makes it polite. You will hear it very often.
sm: ㅑ ㅕ ㅛ ㅠ는 ㅏ ㅓ ㅗ ㅜ 앞에 [y]가 붙은 소리입니다.
ㅑ ㅕ ㅛ ㅠ are ㅏ ㅓ ㅗ ㅜ with [y] in front.

i: ㅗ나 ㅜ에 다른 모음을 붙이면 앞에 [w] 소리가 납니다.
If you join another vowel to ㅗ or ㅜ, a [w] sound (as in "we") comes in front.
w: I bought snacks at the convenience store.
A bag of apples is 5,000 won.
The bus is coming. Get on quickly.
to ride, to get on (a bus, boat)
What are you eating for lunch?
Thank you for showing me the way.
tp: ㅗ는 ㅏ ㅐ와, ㅜ는 ㅓ ㅔ와만 짝이 됩니다.
ㅗ goes only with ㅏ ㅐ, and ㅜ goes only with ㅓ ㅔ.
두 모음을 따로 읽지 말고 한 번에 이어서 소리 냅니다.
Do not read the two vowels separately. Say them together in one sound.
sm: ㅘ ㅝ ㅙ ㅞ는 앞에 [w]가 붙은 소리입니다.
ㅘ ㅝ ㅙ ㅞ are sounds with [w] in front.

i: ㅚ, ㅟ, ㅢ입니다. ㅚ는 ㅙ, ㅞ와 거의 같은 소리로 냅니다.
These are ㅚ, ㅟ, ㅢ. ㅚ sounds almost the same as ㅙ and ㅞ.
w: There are many international students at our school.
My ear hurts, so I go to the hospital.
The key is on the desk.
Today is Sunday, so I rest.
There is no chair. Please give me one.
to not have, to not be (there)
tp: ㅢ는 "으"와 "이"를 빠르게 이어서 냅니다. 입술을 둥글게 하지 않습니다.
For ㅢ, say "으" and "이" quickly together. Do not round your lips.
ㅢ changes its sound by position. At the start of a word it is [의], in other places [이], and "~의" (of, 's) is said [에].
ㅢ changes its sound by position. At the start of a word it is [의], in other places [이], and "~의" (of, 's) is said [에].
dl: No, I am an international student.
sm: ㅚ는 [웨], ㅟ는 [위], ㅢ는 [으이]를 빠르게 낸 소리입니다.
ㅚ sounds like [웨], ㅟ like [위], and ㅢ is [으이] said quickly.

i: 기본 자음 ㄱ ㄴ ㄷ ㄹ ㅁ입니다. 자음은 모음과 함께 써야 소리가 납니다.
These are the basic consonants ㄱ ㄴ ㄷ ㄹ ㅁ. A consonant needs a vowel to make a sound.
l: 가 거 고 구 그 기
나 너 노 누 느 니
다 더 도 두 드 디
라 러 로 루 르 리
마 머 모 무 므 미
w: My older sister is a university student.
My older sister lives in Pakistan.
The weather in my country is hot.
I have a headache. Do you have medicine?
tp: At the start of a word, ㄱ and ㄷ have a little breath, so they can sound like English "k" and "t". Between vowels they sound soft, like "g" and "d".
At the start of a word, ㄱ and ㄷ have a little breath, so they can sound like English "k" and "t". Between vowels they sound soft, like "g" and "d".
ㄹ is between English "r" and "l". Tap the tip of your tongue lightly once, like the "tt" in American "better".
ㄹ is between English "r" and "l". Tap the tip of your tongue lightly once, like the "tt" in American "better".
sm: ㄱ ㄴ ㄷ ㄹ ㅁ sound similar to English g/k, n, d/t, r/l, m.
ㄱ ㄴ ㄷ ㄹ ㅁ sound similar to English g/k, n, d/t, r/l, m.

i: 기본 자음 ㅂ ㅅ ㅇ ㅈ ㅎ입니다.
These are the basic consonants ㅂ ㅅ ㅇ ㅈ ㅎ.
l: 바 버 보 부 브 비
사 서 소 수 스 시
아 어 오 우 으 이
자 저 조 주 즈 지
하 허 호 후 흐 히
w: Can I try on these pants?
to ride, to get on (a bus, boat)
My younger sibling likes the lion doll.
I send money to my father.
I find the way with the map on my phone.
tp: ㅇ has no sound at the start of a syllable. As a final consonant (받침), it sounds like the "ng" in "sing".
ㅇ has no sound at the start of a syllable. As a final consonant (받침), it sounds like the "ng" in "sing".
"시"의 ㅅ은 [s]가 아니라 영어 sh에 가까운 소리가 납니다.
ㅅ in "시" is not [s]; it is close to the English "sh" sound.
dl: to ride, to get on (a bus, boat)
to ride, to get on (a bus, boat)
sm: ㅂ ㅅ ㅈ ㅎ are similar to English b/p, s, j, h, and ㅇ has no sound at the start of a syllable.
ㅂ ㅅ ㅈ ㅎ are similar to English b/p, s, j, h, and ㅇ has no sound at the start of a syllable.

i: ㅋ ㅌ ㅍ ㅊ은 ㄱ ㄷ ㅂ ㅈ에 획을 하나 더한 글자입니다. 숨을 세게 내보내며 소리 냅니다.
ㅋ ㅌ ㅍ ㅊ are ㄱ ㄷ ㅂ ㅈ with one more stroke. Say them with a strong puff of air.
l: 카 커 코 쿠 크 키
타 터 토 투 트 티
파 퍼 포 푸 프 피
ch (with a strong puff of air)
차 처 초 추 츠 치
w: I caught a cold, and my nose is blocked.
How much is a box of tomatoes?
I am going to buy grapes.
Please wash the grapes before you eat them.
to eat, to drink (honorific of 먹다)
Do you have this skirt in another color?
to ride, to get on (a bus, boat)
It takes three hours to Jeonju by train.
tp: At the start of a word, ㅋ ㅌ ㅍ sound almost like English "k", "t", "p" in "kit", "top", "pin" (with a puff of air).
At the start of a word, ㅋ ㅌ ㅍ sound almost like English "k", "t", "p" in "kit", "top", "pin" (with a puff of air).
ㅊ is like the "ch" in "church", with a strong puff of air. In the readings it is written "ch". Do not confuse it with ㅈ (j).
ㅊ is like the "ch" in "church", with a strong puff of air. In the readings it is written "ch". Do not confuse it with ㅈ (j).
입 앞에 얇은 종이를 대고 "카, 타, 파, 차"라고 말해 보세요. 종이가 크게 흔들리면 맞습니다.
Hold a thin piece of paper in front of your mouth and say "카, 타, 파, 차". If the paper moves a lot, you are doing it right.
sm: ㅋ ㅌ ㅍ ㅊ은 숨을 세게 내보내는 소리입니다.
ㅋ ㅌ ㅍ ㅊ are sounds with a strong puff of air.
qz: ㅂ에 획을 더한 글자로, 숨을 세게 내는 것은?
You can read ㅊ like English "s". True → O, false → X

i: ㄲ ㄸ ㅃ ㅆ ㅉ은 같은 자음을 두 번 쓴 글자입니다. 목에 힘을 주고 숨이 나오지 않게 소리 냅니다.
ㄲ ㄸ ㅃ ㅆ ㅉ are the same consonant written twice. Tighten your throat and say them with no puff of air.
l: 까 꺼 꼬 꾸 끄 끼
따 떠 또 뚜 뜨 띠
빠 뻐 뽀 뿌 쁘 삐
싸 써 쏘 쑤 쓰 씨
짜 쩌 쪼 쭈 쯔 찌
w: I give a carrot to the rabbit.
Dad, I arrived in Korea safely.
My older brother is in Korea.
My older brother came to meet me at the airport.
It is a little salty. Some water, please.
tp: ㄲ ㄸ ㅃ are close to the "k", "t", "p" after "s" in English "skin", "stop", "spin" (no puff of air), but tighter.
ㄲ ㄸ ㅃ are close to the "k", "t", "p" after "s" in English "skin", "stop", "spin" (no puff of air), but tighter.
영어를 쓰는 사람은 평음 ㄱ ㄷ ㅂ ㅈ도 조심해야 합니다. 평음은 힘을 빼고 약하게 냅니다.
English speakers should also be careful with the plain sounds ㄱ ㄷ ㅂ ㅈ. Say plain sounds softly, without tension.
dl: Yes, they are cheap. Please come again.
sm: ㄲ ㄸ ㅃ ㅆ ㅉ은 목에 힘을 주고 숨 없이 내는 소리입니다.
ㄲ ㄸ ㅃ ㅆ ㅉ are sounds made with a tight throat and no puff of air.
qz: Which letter is closest to the "t" in English "stop"? ㄷ / ㅌ / ㄸ

i: 글자 아래에 쓰는 자음을 받침이라고 합니다. 먼저 ㅁ과 ㅇ입니다.
A consonant written under a syllable is called 받침 (final consonant). First, ㅁ and ㅇ.
w: I have a video call with my mom.
Do not go out alone at night.
tp: Final ㅁ is like the "m" at the end of English "home", and final ㅇ is like the "ng" in "sing".
Final ㅁ is like the "m" at the end of English "home", and final ㅇ is like the "ng" in "sing".
ㅇ has no sound at the front. It sounds "ng" only as a final consonant. Compare "아" and "앙".
ㅇ has no sound at the front. It sounds "ng" only as a final consonant. Compare "아" and "앙".
dl: I'm going to the library to study.
sm: Final ㅁ sounds "m", and final ㅇ sounds "ng".
Final ㅁ sounds "m", and final ㅇ sounds "ng".

i: 받침 ㄴ과 ㄹ입니다. 받침 ㄹ은 영어 l과 비슷합니다. r처럼 소리 나지 않게 연습하세요.
These are the final consonants ㄴ and ㄹ. Final ㄹ is similar to English "l". Practice so that it does not sound like "r".
w: It snowed a lot, so the road is slippery.
On the weekend, I go to the mountains with my friends.
to not have, to not be (there)
I take out money at the bank.
I have a lot of work.
Today's work ends at five o'clock.
I write my name in Hangul.
tp: For final ㄹ, keep the tip of your tongue on the gum behind your upper teeth. If you say it as "n", "물" sounds like "문", which is a different word.
For final ㄹ, keep the tip of your tongue on the gum behind your upper teeth. If you say it as "n", "물" sounds like "문", which is a different word.
Final ㄴ is the same as the "n" at the end of English words.
Final ㄴ is the same as the "n" at the end of English words.
sm: Final ㄹ is not "n". It is an [l] sound with the tip of the tongue held on the gum.
Final ㄹ is not "n". It is an [l] sound with the tip of the tongue held on the gum.

i: Final ㄱ ㅂ ㄷ are not released: stop the sound and hold it. It is like "k", "p", "t" at the end of "book", "cup", "cat" when you do not let the air out.
Final ㄱ ㅂ ㄷ are not released: stop the sound and hold it. It is like "k", "p", "t" at the end of "book", "cup", "cat" when you do not let the air out.
w: I take my younger sibling to school.
My house is close to the school.
I change into my gym clothes.
I give flowers to my mother.
It is hot during the day, so drink a lot of water.
tp: 받침 ㅅ ㅈ ㅊ ㅌ은 모두 ㄷ 소리로 끝납니다. 옷[옫], 낮[낟], 꽃[꼳].
Final ㅅ ㅈ ㅊ ㅌ all end with a ㄷ (t) sound: 옷[옫], 낮[낟], 꽃[꼳].
받침 뒤에 "으"를 붙여 "채그", "바브"처럼 말하지 않도록 주의합니다.
Be careful not to add "으" after a final consonant, like "채그" or "바브".
sm: Final ㄱ ㅂ ㄷ end with the sound held, like an unreleased "k", "p", "t".
Final ㄱ ㅂ ㄷ end with the sound held, like an unreleased "k", "p", "t".

i: 받침에 자음이 두 개 있는 글자입니다. 낱말만 말할 때는 둘 중 하나만 소리 냅니다.
These syllables have two consonants in the 받침. When you say the word alone, you pronounce only one of them.
w: Half a geun of chicken, please.
geun (unit of weight, 600 g for meat)
Please be sure to read the notice.
I get up at eight in the morning.
I have a lot of work.
There are many customers on weekends.
to not have, to not be (there)
tp: 닭[닥], 여덟[여덜], 값[갑]처럼 하나만 소리 납니다. 어느 쪽인지는 낱말마다 외웁니다.
Only one is pronounced, as in 닭[닥], 여덟[여덜], 값[갑]. Learn which one for each word.
뒤에 모음이 오면 두 번째 자음이 뒤로 넘어가 둘 다 소리 납니다. 읽어요[일거요], 앉아요[안자요].
If a vowel comes after, the second consonant moves to the next syllable and both are pronounced: 읽어요[일거요], 앉아요[안자요].
dl: Thank you. There are a lot of people.
sm: 겹받침은 혼자서는 하나만, 모음 앞에서는 둘 다 소리 납니다.
A double final consonant: alone, only one sounds; before a vowel, both sound.
qz: to not have, to not be (there)

i: 한글은 자음과 모음을 네모 칸 하나에 모아 씁니다. 한 칸이 한 음절입니다.
In Hangul, consonants and vowels are written together in one square block. One block is one syllable.
w: My younger sibling sleeps holding a teddy bear.
to hug, to hold in one's arms
Can I go with you too?
Please lock the door when you go out.
I am going to the hospital tomorrow.
tp: 쓰는 순서는 왼쪽에서 오른쪽, 위에서 아래입니다. 받침은 맨 아래에 씁니다.
Write from left to right and from top to bottom. The 받침 goes at the very bottom.
영어는 글자를 옆으로 한 줄로 쓰지만, 한글 모음은 자음의 오른쪽과 아래에만 옵니다.
English writes letters in one line, but in Hangul the vowel goes only to the right of the consonant or below it.
sm: 한 음절은 자음 + 모음, 또는 자음 + 모음 + 받침으로 만듭니다.
One syllable is consonant + vowel, or consonant + vowel + 받침.

i: 받침 뒤에 ㅇ으로 시작하는 글자가 오면, 받침이 뒤 글자의 첫소리로 넘어갑니다.
When a syllable starting with ㅇ comes after a 받침, the 받침 moves over and becomes the first sound of the next syllable.
w: I can speak a little Korean.
I listen to music while I work.
I eat lunch at a restaurant.
I sit in a seat on the bus.
tp: 글자는 그대로 쓰고 소리만 바뀝니다. 한국어[한구거], 먹어요[머거요], 있어요[이써요].
The spelling stays the same; only the sound changes: 한국어[한구거], 먹어요[머거요], 있어요[이써요].
받침 ㅇ은 넘어가지 않습니다. 가방에[가방에].
Final ㅇ does not move: 가방에[가방에].
sm: 받침은 뒤에 모음이 오면 뒤로 넘어가서 소리 납니다.
When a vowel comes after it, the 받침 moves to the next syllable.

i: 지금까지 배운 글자로 처음 만나는 낱말을 읽어 봅니다.
Let's read some first words with the letters you have learned.
w: I want to work in Korea.
tp: 처음에는 한 글자씩 천천히 읽고, 그다음에 이어서 읽습니다.
At first, read slowly one syllable at a time. Then read them together.
"감사합니다"는 [감사함니다]로 소리 납니다. 이유는 뒤의 발음 규칙 묶음에서 배웁니다.
"감사합니다" is pronounced [감사함니다]. You will learn why in the pronunciation rules unit later.
dl: I am Sam. I am American.
sm: 한글을 다 배웠습니다. 이제 낱말을 읽을 수 있습니다.
You have learned all of Hangul. Now you can read words.

i: ㄱ, ㅋ, ㄲ differ in the strength of the breath and the tension in the throat. English has only one "k" sound, so it is hard to hear ㄱ and ㄲ.
ㄱ, ㅋ, ㄲ differ in the strength of the breath and the tension in the throat. English has only one "k" sound, so it is hard to hear ㄱ and ㄲ.
w: Honey water is good for a cold.
I fold the laundry and put it away.
On the weekend, I dig sweet potatoes with my friends.
We dug potatoes on a field trip.
I broke a plate. I am sorry.
Do you have a bigger size?
tp: ㄲ is like the "k" in "skin" but tighter, and ㅋ is like the "k" in "kit" with a puff of air. ㄱ is in between: say it relaxed and soft, with a low pitch.
ㄲ is like the "k" in "skin" but tighter, and ㅋ is like the "k" in "kit" with a puff of air. ㄱ is in between: say it relaxed and soft, with a low pitch.
낱말 첫머리의 ㄱ 뒤 모음은 낮게, ㅋ과 ㄲ 뒤 모음은 높게 시작합니다. 높낮이로 듣는 것이 가장 쉽습니다.
At the start of a word, the vowel after ㄱ starts low, and the vowel after ㅋ and ㄲ starts high. Listening for high and low pitch is the easiest way.
dl: It is honey. It is sweet.
sm: ㄲ is a tight "k" (as in "skin"), ㅋ is a strong "k" (as in "kit"), and ㄱ is soft and low.
ㄲ is a tight "k" (as in "skin"), ㅋ is a strong "k" (as in "kit"), and ㄱ is soft and low.
qz: Which letter sounds like the "k" in English "kit"? ㄱ / ㅋ / ㄲ

i: These are ㄷ, ㅌ, ㄸ. ㅌ is like the "t" in "top", ㄸ is like the "t" in "stop" but tighter, and ㄷ at the start of a word has a little breath.
These are ㄷ, ㅌ, ㄸ. ㅌ is like the "t" in "top", ㄸ is like the "t" in "stop" but tighter, and ㄷ at the start of a word has a little breath.
w: 용돈은 한 달에 한 번 받아요.
yongdoneun han dare han beon badayo
I get my allowance once a month.
I saw Korean masks at the museum.
I'm the eldest daughter in my family.

English often adds "do" or changes the word order to ask a question, but Korean adds no word. You just raise your voice at the end.
한국어에는 성조가 없습니다. 낱말의 높낮이가 달라도 뜻은 바뀌지 않습니다.
Korean has no tones. Even if the pitch of a word is different, the meaning does not change.
sm: 끝을 올리면 묻는 말, 내리면 답하는 말입니다.
If the end goes up, it is a question; if it goes down, it is an answer.
qz: (소리를 듣고 고르기) 묻는 말 / 답하는 말
한국어는 성조가 있다. 맞으면 O, 틀리면 X

i: "어디, 뭐, 언제"가 있는 물음은 그 낱말을 높고 세게 말하고, 끝은 조금만 올리거나 내립니다.
In questions with "어디, 뭐, 언제", say that word high and strong, and raise or lower the end only a little.
w: Where are you going on the weekend?
Where are you going after class?
What do you do on your day off?
How much is the taxi fare?
tp: Even "어디 가요?" means "어딘가에 가요?" (Are you going somewhere?) if you raise the end high.
Even "어디 가요?" means "Are you going somewhere?" if you raise the end high.
In English, the question word comes at the start of the sentence (Where are you going?), but in Korean it comes right before the verb (어디 가요).
In English, the question word comes at the start of the sentence (Where are you going?), but in Korean it comes right before the verb (어디 가요).
pr: 어디 가요? Where are you going?
어디 가요? ↗ Are you going somewhere?
dl: I am going to a restaurant.
sm: 의문사가 있으면 의문사를 세게 말합니다.
If there is a question word, say it strongly.

i: 같은 "-세요"도 말투에 따라 부탁이 되기도 하고 지시가 되기도 합니다. 학교와 아르바이트하는 곳에서 말투를 알아듣는 연습입니다.
The same "-세요" can be a request or an order, depending on the tone. Let's practice hearing the tone at school and at a part-time job.
w: Wash your hands well before you do it.
Please separate your recycling in the dormitory.
Please do your course registration by tomorrow.
Just a moment, I'll write it down.
to write down, to take a note
tp: 끝을 부드럽게 늘이면 부탁, 짧고 세게 끊으면 지시입니다.
If the end is soft and long, it is a request. If it is short and strong, it is an order.
한국 사람의 빠르고 센 말투는 화난 것이 아니라 급하다는 뜻일 때가 많습니다.
When Koreans speak fast and strongly, it often means they are in a hurry, not angry.
dl: Just a moment. Please help me with this.
sm: 부드럽게 늘이면 부탁, 짧게 끊으면 지시입니다.
Soft and long is a request; short and cut off is an order.
qz: 표지와 안내 방송에서 쓰는 말투는? 하세요 / 하십시오

i: 지금까지 배운 헷갈리는 소리의 짝을 다시 듣고 고릅니다.
Listen again to the confusing pairs of sounds you have learned and choose.
w: to turn on (a light, a machine)
There is a lot of grass.
I stick the documents with glue.
The water is not coming out.
to happen (고장이 나다 = to break down)
I gained weight after coming to Korea.
tp: Three things English speakers should be most careful about: tell apart plain, strong and tight sounds (ㄱ ㅋ ㄲ), do not add a vowel after a final consonant, and do not say ㅓ and ㅗ (or ㅡ and ㅜ) the same.

Three things English speakers should be most careful about: tell apart plain, strong and tight sounds (ㄱ ㅋ ㄲ), do not add a vowel after a final consonant, and do not say ㅓ and ㅗ (or ㅡ and ㅜ) the same.
글자와 소리가 다른 곳은 연음, 콧소리, 된소리, 거센소리 네 가지 규칙으로 거의 다 설명됩니다.
Almost every place where spelling and sound differ can be explained by four rules: linking, nasal sounds, tense sounds, and strong (aspirated) sounds.
dl: Did you turn off the light?
Yes, I closed the door too.
sm: 헷갈리는 소리는 짝으로 듣고 말하며 익힙니다.
Learn confusing sounds by listening and speaking in pairs.
